title: Adaptive Request Shaping Initiative — Cost Control through Dynamic Batching, KV Prefetch, and Mixed-Precision Profiles
creator: Nina Ortega
description:
Problem statement: Hosting customers require predictable unit economics while maintaining strict latency SLOs. Existing static batching + quant profiles produce uneven savings across workloads and cause regression surface in tail latency. This initiative will build an adaptive request-shaping framework that dynamically adjusts batching windows, issues KV-prefetch hints for repeated prefixes, and selects mixed-precision execution profiles per-request class to reduce per-token cost without violating SLOs.

Goals:
- Deliver a production-safe control plane + runtime hooks to make dynamic batching and kv-prefetch decisions per-route.
- Provide quantization profile selection (fp16/4-bit hybrid) that can be evaluated and rolled out per-customer or per-route.
- Produce tooling and dashboards to measure token-econ delta, latency tail regressions, and rollback triggers tied to prompt-test suites.

Why different: Rather than a one-size playbook, this effort treats request shaping as a runtime policy surfaced in the Console (policy templates + canary rules) and enforced in the serving runtime with observability and automatic fallback policies.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes a per-route policy API for dynamic batch windows and prefetched KV hints
End-to-end tests validate <2.5% p99 latency regression for 95% of tested prompt suites when adaptive policies are enabled
Console UI surfaces per-route token-econ delta and a single-click canary rollout/rollback
Automated guardrail that falls back to baseline model variant when latency or error thresholds breached
Quantization profile selection integrated with rollout system and observable in traces/dashboards
